transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net business technical support. My name is Liam. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Liam. I'm calling from an architecture firm in Leeds. We have an S-Net Business Pro broadband line, and we need to get a dedicated static IPv4 address assigned and set up a reverse DNS PTR record for our outgoing mail server.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly assist you with static IP routing and reverse DNS configuration, Nadia. Before we access the network records, may I please verify your company billing address and the security question answer on the account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Of course. The address is Studio 4, Wharf Road, Leeds, LS11 5QZ. And the security question is our primary director's mother's maiden name, which is Gallagher.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Nadia, that fully verifies the account. Can you tell me what domain name you are delegating for the PTR record?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We are getting completely blocked by major spam filtering networks because our mail server IP resolves to a generic dynamic pool hostname! All our architectural client proposals are bouncing back right now, and our directors are in a total panic!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the urgency when client emails and proposals are bouncing back, Nadia. Having critical business mail rejected by spam filters is extremely stressful for any enterprise, so let us get this resolved right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much Liam, that is a huge relief to know you can help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your outgoing mail server is currently utilizing a dynamic WAN address that lacks reverse DNS alignment, triggering spam filter rejections, and you require a dedicated static IP bound with a custom PTR record pointing to mail.wharf-architects.co.uk. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what we need. The fully qualified hostname is mail.wharf-architects.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am checking our regional IP pool allocations for the Leeds central exchange. I have an available /32 static IP address ready to reserve: 194.74.82.115.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me write that down: 194.74.82.115. Will that bind to our existing S-Net Business Hub automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Our radius authentication server maps the static reservation to your broadband login credentials, so your router will receive this identical IP on every session restart.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very convenient. Do I need to reconfigure the gateway and subnet mask on our internal firewall?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The gateway remains 194.74.82.1 with a single-host 255.255.255.255 subnet mask on the router WAN interface, while your internal LAN operates on standard 192.168.1.0/24.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it. And what about the PTR record on the authoritative nameserver?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am opening the S-Net Master DNS registry console now to create the in-addr.arpa delegation for 115.82.74.194.in-addr.arpa.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long will it take before external servers can see that PTR record?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you don't even know basic DNS propagation principles, maybe you shouldn't be attempting to run an on-premises mail server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me? That was completely uncalled for. I am the IT coordinator managing twenty people, not a full-time DNS specialist. I just asked a straightforward question.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It takes two to four hours for regional DNS caches to expire their TTL and refresh the new zone record across authoritative resolvers worldwide.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. Two to four hours is all I wanted to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The PTR record for 194.74.82.115 has now been committed to our primary nameservers ns1.snet-business.net and ns2.snet-business.net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we test resolving it locally from command prompt right now to verify the syntax?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Please open your command prompt on your workstation and type: nslookup 194.74.82.115 ns1.snet-business.net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running the nslookup query against your primary nameserver... it responds: 115.82.74.194.in-addr.arpa name = mail.wharf-architects.co.uk!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The authoritative zone file has accepted the entry without syntax error.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's great. What about the forward DNS A record on our domain registrar?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You must log into your domain registrar, such as GoDaddy or 123 Reg, and ensure the A record for mail.wharf-architects.co.uk points to 194.74.82.115.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have our domain management portal open right here. Updating the A record host 'mail' to 194.74.82.115 with a 300-second TTL right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Saving that completes Forward-Confirmed reverse DNS, which ensures full compliance with Spamhaus and Google anti-spoofing policies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just saved. Now, do we need to check port 25 outbound on our S-Net business line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unlike residential packages which filter SMTP traffic, S-Net Business Pro broadband lines keep outbound TCP port 25 unblocked by default.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test telnetting to an external mail host on port 25... connected immediately with 220 banner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms bidirectional SMTP connectivity is open without line restriction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should we also verify our SPF TXT record syntax?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your SPF string should include 'ip4:194.74.82.115' followed by '~all' or '-all' to authorize this IP.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking our DNS control panel... yes, v=spf1 ip4:194.74.82.115 ~all is present.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What about your DKIM cryptographic signing keys on the outgoing mail daemon?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: DKIM is generated on our mail server and published as a 2048-bit RSA public key TXT record on the domain.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Having both SPF and DKIM aligned with rDNS guarantees maximum deliverability into Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace inboxes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is exactly what we need to ensure our architectural tender submissions do not end up in junk folders.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, do we need to reboot your S-Net Business Hub to bind the static IP address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please trigger the restart whenever you are ready.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will trigger an administrative PPP session renegotiation from our portal right now, which takes about sixty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, the hub lights are flickering amber as the connection renegotiates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The PPP session has re-established with IP address 194.74.82.115. Please check the WAN IP displayed in your router admin panel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refreshing the router overview page... yes! Public IP address is showing 194.74.82.115, subnet 255.255.255.255.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check, Nadia, is your office local area network and internal file server communication running normally across all workstations?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our internal gigabit network and NAS shares are completely unaffected, all architects can access CAD files.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now please test sending an outbound test email from your mail client to an external test recipient such as a Gmail address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am sending a test message to my personal Gmail account right now... hitting Send.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us inspect the incoming message headers once received to confirm SPF, DKIM, and rDNS alignment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The email just landed in my Gmail inbox! Checking 'Show Original' headers: SPF PASS, DKIM PASS, and Received from 194.74.82.115 matches mail.wharf-architects.co.uk!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the mail server delivery chain is fully verified and will not trigger spam filters.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What a massive relief. Our architects can send proposals again without bouncing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked this static IP reservation permanently to your S-Net Business Pro account ID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for getting the IP and DNS sorting out, Liam.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your S-Net business broadband line or static routing that I can assist you with today, Nadia?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that resolves our mail delivery problem completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a short automated survey following this call; we would appreciate any feedback on your technical support experience today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will complete the survey. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net Business, Nadia. Goodbye.
